build_inputs.angles:
- 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft from a twin-turbo 5.5-litre flat-plane V8 that revs to 8,000, and 233 miles an hour.
- It makes more power than a Ferrari SF90 or a Lamborghini Revuelto, both of which cost about three times as much.
- For 67 years the engine sat in front of the driver. The C8 put it behind them in 2020, and that is the only reason a car like this exists.
- Zora Arkus-Duntov wanted it there in 1957, after the Corvette SS broke at Sebring and he worked out the heat had to go behind the driver. GM said no for five decades.

sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 2026 Chevrolet Corvette ZR1 Coupe 3LZ, finished in Arctic White with an Asymmetrical Adrenaline Red and Jet Black interior. The odometer on this Corvette ZR1 currently displays approximately 2,200 miles. The attached Carfax vehicle history report shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies in this ZR1’s brief past. According to the window sticker provided in the gallery, this ZR1 cost $224,085 new, including over $30,000 in options. A partial list of notable equipment includes the ZR1 Carbon Fiber Aero Package, Carbon Fiber Interior Trim Level 2 Package, forged aluminum wheels, carbon ceramic brakes, Magnetic Selective Ride Control, heated and ventilated seats, a Bose sound system, and front lift adjustable height memory. The seller reports no notable modifications. The eighth-generation Corvette ZR1 builds on the legacy of Chevrolet’s high-performance sports cars, representing the most powerful and advanced production Corvette to date. As a convertible, it offers open-air driving without sacrificing structural rigidity or performance. The ZR1 designation has historically signified top-tier performance and exclusivity within the Corvette lineup, appealing to enthusiasts seeking advanced technology and track-capable engineering. Power comes from a 5.5-liter twin-turbocharged V8, rated at 1,064 horsepower and 828 lb-ft of torque. Output is sent to the rear wheels via an 8-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
